user_questions.question: Q1: No Salesforce object holds food orders (orders live in the external Pronto Orders API). Where should actual prep time per order be recorded? (A) new custom object child of Storefront__c keyed by external order number [recommended]; (B) extend Transaction__c (sales/refunds, no storefront link) with a storefront lookup and prep fields; (C) keep it only in the external system and store just the SLA in Salesforce. Q2: How should 'measure it' be delivered? (A) per-order breach flag only; (B) breach flag plus a per-storefront breach-rate report [recommended].
user_questions.simulated_answer: Q1: No preference; use your recommended default. Target prep minutes on Storefront; actual prep time per order. Q2: A breach-rate report.

skill_friction: Step 5 says a fork must be asked only when neither requirement nor evidence gives a basis to choose; here evidence (no order object, Transaction__c is sales/refunds) did favour a new object, so asking Q1 was borderline. The skill does not say whether a 'new object vs repurpose existing object' fork counts as 'two interpretations need different objects' when one option is clearly better.

Whether a report counts as a required deliverable of 'measure it' is ambiguous; the skill gives no guidance on reporting deliverables (Report, ReportType, ReportFolder) or on reusing auto-generated report types and unfiled$public.

AskCoworker D1 missed Transaction__c and claimed 'Verified' absence of any order-like object; the only way to catch this was an unprompted sobject list scan. The skill could make a full custom object list scan an explicit step after D1.
AskCoworker answers repeatedly cited 'prior session' as verification despite the ignore-earlier-conversations header; the handling table covers this but it made every [Verified] tag unreliable.

Formula blank-handling (BlankAsZero vs BlankAsBlank) materially changed breach results, and AskCoworker got it wrong; the org-verification reference has no guidance for checking formula edge cases on fields that do not exist yet.
